tool.name: Collection anchor grid
tool.description: anchor x query chain selection + relabel map for the TOGA2 pass

param.name: anchors
param.label: Anchor collection
param.help: Genomes that donate annotation. Their element identifiers form the target side of the wanted chains.

param.name: strains
param.label: Strain (query) collection
param.help: The full panel. Anchors must also appear here, since WF-C only produced chains for panel members.

tool.help:
Bridges WF-C's chain collection onto WF-C2's projection grid.
WF-C emits one cleaned chain per ordered strain pair, keyed ``{target}.{query}`` (56 cells for 8 strains). WF-C2's grid is anchors x strains with the anchor self-cells dropped, keyed ``{anchor}_{query}`` (21 cells for 3 anchors x 8 strains). TOGA2's ``--chain_file`` is the reference-to-query chain and its reference is the anchor, so cell ``{anchor}_{query}`` needs the chain whose **target** is the anchor, i.e. ``{anchor}.{query}``.
This emits the two files that bridge them:
- **chain ids to keep** — one ``{anchor}.{query}`` per line, for ``__FILTER_FROM_FILE__`` with ``remove_if_absent``. - **chain relabel map** — ``{anchor}.{query}<TAB>{anchor}_{query}``, for ``__RELABEL_FROM_FILE__``. - **grid order** — ``{anchor}_{query}`` in cross-product order, for ``__SORTLIST__`` with ``sort_type: file``. Galaxy pairs collections in a map-over by **position**, not by identifier: the other grids are in anchor-collection order while chains filtered out of WF-C keep WF-C's alphabetical order, so without this every cell receives another cell's chain.
Both are derived from the two collections' element identifiers, so a new panel needs no hand-authored config. Fails loudly if an anchor is not also a member of the strain collection, since WF-C would never have produced its chains.
